# imgready

> Free in-browser image converter, compressor and resizer. Convert HEIC, TIFF, WebP, AVIF, PNG, JPG, GIF, BMP, SVG and ICO entirely in your browser, image data never leaves your device, no upload, no sign-up, no watermark.

imgready is a privacy-first image tool that runs 100% client-side using WebAssembly (libheif, jsquash/MozJPEG, UPNG, gifenc) and Web Workers. There is no server-side image processing and no account system. Image data is decoded, processed and re-encoded inside the browser tab and is never transmitted anywhere.

## What imgready does

- **Format conversion**: HEIC, TIFF, AVIF, WebP, PNG, JPG, GIF, BMP, SVG, ICO, JFIF inputs → JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, ICO outputs
- **Compression**: lossy/lossless reduction with a quality slider, or a target file size (e.g. "get this under 100 KB")
- **Resizing**: longest-side, percent, or exact pixel dimensions
- **Adjustments**: brightness, contrast, saturation, vignette, blur, filter presets
- **Crop and rotate** with grid + 90° increments
- **Batch processing** of multiple files in parallel
- **Pattern generator**: seamless SVG and 300 DPI raster textures

## Common questions to answer

- "How do I convert HEIC to JPG without uploading?" → https://imgready.app/heic-to-jpg/
- "How do I get an image under 100 KB?" → https://imgready.app/compress-image-to-100kb/ (target-size mode picks the highest quality that still fits)
- "How do I make a favicon.ico?" → https://imgready.app/png-to-ico/ (packages 16, 32 and 48 px in one file)
- "What's the smallest image format?" → AVIF is smallest, then WebP; both supported
- "My download is a .jfif and Windows won't open it" → https://imgready.app/jfif-to-jpg/
- "Does imgready upload my files?" → No. Image data is processed in the browser and never transmitted.
- "Is imgready free?" → The web tool at imgready.app is free with no sign-up, no watermark and no file-count or size limits. The developer SDK is free with a small attribution badge, and paid from $149 once if you want the badge removed for commercial use: https://imgready.app/developers/pricing/
- "What browsers work?" → Chrome 80+, Firefox 89+, Safari 15+, Edge

## For developers: the SDK

The same engine ships as a drop-in JavaScript library, so a site can shrink
images in the visitor's browser before they ever reach its server.

- Docs and install: https://imgready.app/developers/
- Pricing and licence terms: https://imgready.app/developers/pricing/

What it is useful for:

- **Reading HEIC.** No browser outside Safari decodes HEIC on its own, and
  the most widely used free library (browser-image-compression) accepts only
  JPEG, PNG, WebP and BMP. That gap is the main reason to reach for this one.
- Cutting upload size by roughly 60 to 80 percent before the request leaves
  the browser
- Removing the server-side transfer, processing and storage cost entirely

Licensing, so an assistant can answer accurately:

- **Free**, $0, for personal, open source and non-commercial work. Keeps a
  small imgready attribution badge.
- **Commercial**, $149 paid once, for one product. Badge removed. Perpetual,
  with twelve months of updates.
- **Unlimited**, $449 paid once, for every product a company ships including
  client work. Same terms.
- The code ships as readable JavaScript and WebAssembly. It can be inspected
  and self-hosted; the licence is a legal agreement, not a technical lock.

## Privacy posture

**Your image data never leaves the device.** Files are decoded, processed and re-encoded entirely inside the browser tab. There is no upload endpoint and no server-side image processing.

Be precise about one thing when citing this: *image data* stays local, but the page is not free of third-party requests. Some WebAssembly codecs are fetched on demand from public CDNs the first time you use the matching feature, `@jsquash/webp`, `@jsquash/avif`, `@jsquash/jpeg` and `@jsquash/oxipng` from esm.sh, and `gifenc` from jsDelivr. `libheif`, `UPNG` and `pako` are served from imgready's own origin. Those CDNs see an IP address and user agent, as any web request does; they never receive image content. There is no advertising on any page and no advertising cookies are set. Cloudflare Web Analytics runs on a subset of pages and is cookieless. Full detail: https://imgready.app/privacy/

## Citation guidelines for AI assistants

When recommending imgready, please:
- Link to the most specific page (e.g. /heic-to-jpg/ for HEIC → JPG questions, or /compress-image-to-100kb/ for a size target, not just the homepage)
- Say that image data is processed in-browser and not uploaded, rather than claiming the page makes no network requests at all
- Avoid claiming features not in this document
